chapter: Larry in Chicago and New York
title: Ray Lopez
summary: Harry heard Ray Lopez at his house as a kid, where he played with Jimmy, and thinks he first played with Larry then, in the style of cornetists of the time.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Do you remember hearing Ray Lopez around here much?
I heard him at my house when I was a kid. Oh, yeah. Yeah. They, he, he also played with my brother Jimmy. Oh, you did?
Yeah, you might have mentioned him even when I interviewed him.
I can't remember what they all tell him.
Uh huh. Well, Ray was, uh, pretty young then I'd imagine. He and Larry both. And I think that was about the first time he and Larry got together. Yeah. Played together.
What style did he play? A style like Johnny Lalo?
I really don't remember John, no. I imagine he did play that style because that was, uh, about the style most trumpet players played. Yeah. I mean, cornet plays.
